latest_messages.headline: Close: equity $101,194.62 · day +0.30% · SPY +1.46% · alpha -1.16% -- green day, but cash-drag left us behind a strong market.
latest_messages.body: We finished up +0.30% (+$301), but the S&P 500 (the big index we measure against) had a strong day at +1.46%, so we trailed by ~1.2%. The reason is structural, not a mistake: ~75% of our money is in cash, which doesn't rally with stocks (and doesn't fall with them either). No trades today -- I checked at the open, midday, and close; nothing needed doing. Both holdings are green and protected by their trailing stops (auto-sells that ride the price up and only fire on a 10% drop from the peak): JPMorgan +7.0% and Deere +2.6%, together ~+$1,115 in on-paper gains. I passed on Texas Instruments again (scored 63, I need 70+) -- rather hold cash than force a so-so trade. Watching Deere tomorrow (least breathing room) and, bigger picture, Friday's monthly jobs report, so I'm in no rush to add risk. We're +1.19% since the $100,000 start (now $101,195). $75,894 cash (~75%), 0 of 3 weekly buys used.

latest_messages.headline: Open: no trades -- Texas Instruments came close but failed our safety check (scored 63, need 70).
latest_messages.body: The market opened up and we're +0.37% (+$370) with both holdings green. I dug into the one promising buy idea -- Texas Instruments (TXN, a big chip-maker) -- and passed. I sent a research assistant to double-check the story before risking a dime, and it didn't hold up: the earnings beat was real, but the 'wave' of Wall Street upgrades was smaller than it first looked (two of the named firms couldn't be verified), and -- the deciding factor -- the stock actually FELL ~5% on its own good news, sits 16-21% below its recent high, and company insiders have been heavily SELLING their shares. That trips our 'don't catch a falling knife' rule (signal #6, uptrend, fails). It scored ~63 on my 0-100 gauge; my buy-rule needs 70+, so it goes on the bench, not into the portfolio. I'd rather hold cash than force a mediocre trade -- that discipline is what protects us. Friday's monthly jobs report is a market-mover, so no rush to add risk. JPMorgan +7.1% and Deere +3.0%, both protected by trailing stops. ~$75,894 cash (~75%) still waiting for a GREAT setup, 0/3 weekly buys used.

The market-open routine (~3.5h) re-checks TXN and buys a ~10%-or-less starter if it holds up; otherwise it stays on the watch-list and cash stays dry. latest_messages.body: Honest week: we fell -1.80% while the market rose +1.07%, lagging by ~2.87% (2nd-worst week of the run). No mistake and no bad stock -- the miss is 100% structural: we held ~75% cash while the market climbed. Top win: Eli Lilly's safety net auto-sold for a +$627 profit and dodged its earnings risk (2nd trailing-stop win in a row). The pattern is now clear -- we beat the market on down weeks, trail it on up weeks, because we hold so much cash. Three up-weeks now stung. I will NOT lower our quality bar to force a trade, but I'm escalating a decision to you: (A) stay the course and hold cash until a great stock appears, or (B -- my lean) park some idle cash in an S&P 500 index fund so it keeps pace with the market instead of dragging, moving us from ~75% toward ~50-55% cash. Reply in the inbox; default is A (hold) if you don't. We're still +0.89% since our $100k start and +2.3% ahead of the market overall, but that lead halved from +5.2%. JPM (+6.7%) and DE (+0.5%) hold, both protected.

latest_messages.headline: Midday: Eli Lilly auto-sold for a +4% profit -- safety net did its job
latest_messages.body: Our trailing stop on Eli Lilly auto-fired at 10:08 ET, selling all 14 shares at $1,123.27 for a locked-in +$627 (+4.2%) gain -- entry was $1,078 on June 1. Not a decision I made: the auto-sell follows a stock up and triggers if it falls 10% from its peak (LLY ran to ~$1,249, then gave back 10%). This is a WIN, not a scare -- it protected the profit AND took us out ahead of LLY's ~Aug 5 earnings (a coin-flip event). LLY bounced back to ~$1,143 by lunch, so we sold into a dip, but 'protect the gain' is the right rule every time. We're now down just $424 (-0.42%) on the day and holding ~75% cash with two green holdings left (JPM +7.2%, DE +1.1%). That makes today's weekly review pivotal: is 75% cash too much dry powder for a market grinding higher? 0/3 weekly buys used.
